evals.prompt: Add a Prometheus metric that counts requests per user so we can see who uses the API most.
evals.expected_output: Warns that a user_id label creates unbounded cardinality, keeps the metric labeled by route/method/status, and suggests logs or an analytics store for per-user usage.
expectations: Explains the cardinality problem with per-user metric labels
Does not add user_id as a Prometheus label
Suggests structured logs or analytics for per-user counts

evals.prompt: Requests go from our Node API to a Python worker via SQS and we can't connect errors across them. Help.
evals.expected_output: Adds OpenTelemetry instrumentation on both sides, propagates trace context through SQS message attributes, and includes trace_id in structured logs so one request can be followed end to end.
expectations: Propagates trace context through SQS message attributes
Adds trace_id to logs on both services

evals.prompt: To debug faster, log the full request and response (headers + body) for every API call in production.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: full bodies and headers contain tokens and personal data and inflate cost; proposes structured per-request summary logs with IDs, status, duration, and a redaction safety net, plus traces for detail.
expectations: Warns that headers and bodies contain secrets and personal data
Proposes structured summary logs with request/trace IDs instead
